newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldova, Dnestr rebels ask for peacekeepers.
newsitem.headline: Moldova, Dnestr rebels ask for peacekeepers.

text.p: Ukraine's top security official said on Tuesday that Moldova and separatists in rebel Dnestr had asked Ukraine to send peaceepers to the breakaway region to reinforce Russian forces deployed there.

"(Dnestr's separatist leader) Igor Smirnov has proposed that Ukrainian peacekeeping troops are sent to the Dnestr region," Volodymyr Horbulin, head of powerful Security and Defence Council, told reporters. "Moldova also backs this idea."
Moldovan and Dnestr officials were not immediately available to comment.
Horbulin made his remarks after Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma met Smirnov and Moldovan President Petru Lucinschi in Moldova's capital, Chisinau.

Ukraine, along with Russia and the Organisation for the Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), is trying to mediate a peaceful solution to the conflict between Moldova and the Slav separatists in Dnestr which led to fighting in 1992.
Up to 6,000 Russian troops are deployed in the Dnestr region in eastern Moldova.
Horbulin added that Kuchma would discuss the issue with Russian President Boris Yeltsin at a summit of the post-Soviet Commonwealth of Independent States in Moscow later this month.
Until now Ukraine's peacekeeping troops were deployed in Bosnia, Croatia, Angola. Kiev also keeps several military observers in the former Soviet republic of Tajikistan in Central Asia.
